As good as it is to see more female firefighers, I find the "omg a female firefighter" a bit annoying everytime one joins the ranks.

I like to look at it from the point of view as it's a celebration or encouragement for other young girls to feel encouraged to enter the field as well.

I feel like the fact we can still say "As good as it is to see more female firefighters..." indicates it's still a male dominated field, and it is encouraging to hear of another one making it into the ranks and being successful.

Completely agree if the story was tinted slightly differently, e.g. "Look, somehow this girl managed to do 'man's work'!" then I would be a bit peeved, but I think this article had a fairly positive spin.

I like to think if I wouldn't praise a man for it, I wouldn't praise a woman for it. To me, that's equality.

I also think it can be quite patronizing when people lump someone's achievements with their gender, so I think that might be the annoying feeling. Especially when the praise is heaped on way too strong - it makes it seem like its a monumental task for women to accomplish. Or like women are children. As if it's somehow unexpected or unprecedented for a woman to become a firefighter - I don't think it is.

Despite all that, I do think young girls need more non-actress/singer/model role models so maybe it is a good thing, but perhaps only when they've accomplished something that a man would be praised for?

That's a rally interesting way to put it. I hadn't thought of it as praise, but more of excitement that the standard "firefighter" stereotype is broadening so when people think of firefight firefighters they wouldn't automatically assume it's a man. It's the same excitement I have when men pursue a career as a nurse or make-up artist-- it's not meant to be a patronizing "Oh good for you, you're just as good as the other gender!" But more of a "I'm so excited stereotypical-gendered careers are broadening how people will see these career"

The thing for me is that women have been breaking these stereotypes for years. My mom was one of 2 women in her Geology cohort of 20 back in the 1970s. Where's her article? I think someone else mentioned in this thread that there are also plenty of other women firefighters in Australia. People just need to open their eyes and look around.

The second thing is I'm really not too hot on the idea of celebrating people "breaking stereotypes" in this day and age and not in a country like Australia where people are free to do what they want (as evidenced by other female firefighters) by and large. I think its a sign of independent thought and to me that should be the minimum expectation of everyone - you do what you want, not what society wants.

Another thing I'm concerned about is I heard from a woman who works in the Australian Defence Force that women in the army for example are really scared of being celebrated simply because they're women because they don't want to be perceived as unqualified and they want to earn respect on the same terms as the men. So in that sense praising/celebrating them for things men don't get praised for is quite a sensitive issue for them as it can cause resentment/friction issues within their units. I'm not sure if its the same for firefighters, but I think I share that view. If people started adding "female" in front of my job title, or when telling people how well I do my job, I would be freaked out.

It's also the tone - this article was fairly benign but there are some articles that go full-on sycophantic and offering praise that is really hyperbolic. I think that type of thing annoys OP.

Like I said earlier given that more American middle schoolers would prefer to be a celebrity's assistant than the president of Harvard, I'm always happy to see women in other fields than entertainment being promoted. But in this case, what has this particular woman done that hundreds and thousands of women before her haven't?
Lol you should see the bullshit my sisters deal with. Both of 'em wake up get to the jobsite at 6:30 am to start insulating chill water and air ducts.
Articles like these are what make people mad. As long as they can maintain a standard, it's okay, but if they fail.... hopefully they don't put her on a ladder and endanger people's lives

I'm just gonna sit by the pool and enjoy a drink of my own creation:

The Snow Flower

  • 1.5 oz. Barcardi Mango Fusion
  • 1.5 oz. Bacardi Pineapple Fusion
  • 1.0 oz. Fresh Squeezed Lemon Juice
  • 0.5 oz. Water
  • 2 Tbsp Superfine Sugar

Rim 12 oz. Rocks Glass with sugar, and fill with ice. Fill mixing tin half way full with ice. Add ingredients in order, and shake 10-12 times. Strain over fresh ice. Garnish with Lemon

Enjoy!

This drink is inspired by the classic Lemon Drop, and therefore can be made as a cocktail (shown,) as a shot, or as a Martini with only slight variations.
